correctness.rationale: Angular Parseval and the radial beta integral give the reciprocal squared monomial norms Γ(t+2n+3)/(2πΓ(t+1)Γ(2n+2)), with polynomial growth in n for fixed t. The coefficient determinant, up to positive row and column factors, is an Andréief integral of two generalized Vandermondes against the positive product weight x²e⁻ˣ dx. Both determinants have the same strict positive sign on the increasingly ordered chamber (exponential Chebyshev systems after log x); the integrals converge for t>−1. Finite Cauchy–Binet expresses each radial minor as a sum of nonnegative terms; continuity covers a radial node of zero, and the consecutive-power term is strictly positive and independent of the truncation. Entrywise convergence preserves that lower bound. The ratio inequality follows from the order-two minor, and the distinct-zero bound follows from invertibility of any k-node evaluation matrix.
residual_risks: The replay is finite and tests integer t; real t and all orders are covered by the determinant argument, not by sampling.

value.rationale: This compares radial evaluation across weights in the natural power-of-distance family. Beyond order-two monotonicity, it guarantees nonsingular interpolation matrices and a uniform distinct-zero bound for any finite mixture of the radial profiles. Those are structural facts not supplied by the exact scalar formula, its complex zeros, or parameter regularity alone.
residual_risks: No off-diagonal total positivity, multiplicity bound, or extension to general domains is asserted.
